text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski has signed the new penal code which does away with death penalty.

- Poland's Supreme Court has rejected a motion by two Solidarity Election Action (AWS) leaders Adam Slomka and Janusz Tomaszewski who questioned the legality of results of the constitutional referendum on May 25.
- The ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) plans to challenge the recently passed vetting act at the Constitutional Tribunal on Friday, the SLD said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- "I am going to promote NATO expansion at the US Senate," the former US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger said at a presentation of the Polish Great Order of Merit from President Kwasniewski on Thursday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's treasury ministry will produce a privatisation timetable for Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist, by the end of July, treasury ministry spokesman Zbigniew Ostrowski said.

- Around 87 million foreigners visited Poland in 1996, showing a 6.3 percent increase from the year before, a report by the tourist office presented to the cabinet's social and economic committee (KSERM) said.
- The ZA Pulawy fertiliser maker will complete in September its production line modernisation and development programme which took several years and cost 180 million zlotys, the company said.
- The state-owned Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) and Bud-Bank SA have agreed to jointly credit housing development schemes, the banks said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- A group of Polish investors has bought an 85.5 percent stake in the KIB Bank in Kharkov, Ukraine. The bank is participating in the first stage of an export contract of 50 Polish-made Bizon combine harvesters to Ukraine, Piotr Bykowski, supervisory board president of the export investment guarantee foundation (FPIE) said.
- H. Bauer, Gruner +Jahr and Axel Springer are Poland's biggest press publishers, a report by the SMG/KRC market research agency said.

- The Swiss Juerg Marquard publishing will suspend issuing the Sztandar Mlodych daily on July 25 due to bad financial results if it does not sell the newspaper by that date, Sztandar's deputy chief editor Grazyna Minkowska said.

- Poland's customs office has not reported any attempts to import English beef to Poland, which is still banned due to the Britain's mad-cow disease issue, the agriculture ministry veterinary department official Barbara Wirska said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Polish customers contracted over 10,000 Siena Fiat cars in the first two days of the offer, Fiat Auto Poland official Giovanni Prati said.
- The Texaco Poland fuel distributor will shortly launch a franchising programme addressed to private petrol station operators, the company said.

- Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH), the state treasury and the industrial development agency (ARP) have agreed to write off 85 percent of the Bumar Labedy armament maker's liabilities totalling 175 million zlotys.
ZYCIE

- Average gross monthly salary in Poland's public sector reached 1,067 zlotys in the first five months of 1997 showing a 20.8 percent upturn on the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
